entries.title: I Kings 13:1
segments:
By the word of the Lord; at his command. 
 
Shrewd worldly politicians know that men must have some religion, and they encourage that which they think will increase and perpetuate their power.  But in substituting one of their own devising for that which God requires, they incur his wrath and accelerate their own ruin.

entries.title: I Kings 13:2
segments: Offer the priests of the high places; kill them, and burn their bones on the altar.
Men's bones shall be burnt upon thee; the bones of men long since dead.

entries.title: I Kings 13:3
segments: A sign; a miracle, to show that God had sent him.
When God sends a message to men, he gives such evidence that it comes from him as ought to convince, and if rightly treated, will convince them; and if it does not, it is their own fault.

entries.title: I Kings 13:6
segments: God can easily and quickly bring the most bitter persecutors of his people into such a condition that they will earnestly desire and implore their help.

entries.title: I Kings 13:8
segments: The messengers of God should show that they regard him more than all earthly good, and no temptations should induce them to swerve from following his directions.

entries.title: I Kings 13:15
segments: God's people are sometimes tempted to disobey him, but they are never forced to do it; and if they do it, they displease him, and subject themselves to his rebuke.

entries.title: I Kings 13:19
segments:
He went back; instead of following the command of God: he had received his directions from God, and had no right to deviate from them until God himself had countermanded them.  That God had done so, he had no sufficient evidence. 
 
When God has clearly made known his will, we are not to follow the opposing counsels of men, however plausible they may seem.

entries.title: I Kings 13:24
segments: As no one knows the time or manner of his death, all should so live as to be prepared at any time to meet it, and hear the joyful sentence, Well done, good and faithful servant; enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.

entries.title: I Kings 13:30
segments: When those we have injured are dead, the recollection of our influence over them often gives us poignant sorrow.

entries.title: I Kings 13:32
segments: Samaria; a part of Canaan which lay between Judea and Galilee.

entries.title: I Kings 13:33
segments: We are often reminded that no mercies or judgments, promises or threatenings, without the grace of God, will lead men to forsake their sins and turn to him; and that whatever be his dealings, they will continue in transgression till they perish.
